Second review of the library catalog and keeps(q) -- 1.24.38, branch wip-2026-11-24-library at 43135ea
==================================================================================================

Written without seeing the first review's cases or the drafting. Cases: cases.js (426), run by replay.js;
the 60 labelled questions of part D: questions.json.

  node tests/fixtures/review2_library_1238/replay.js                 -> 426 cases: 319 AGREE, 107 DISAGREE
      (14 high, 54 medium, 39 low)
  node tests/fixtures/review2_library_1238/replay.js <1.24.37 file>  -> 426 cases: 327 AGREE, 99 DISAGREE
      (the old file has no keeps() and no OPEN: it misses the food questions A01-A29 and every command in B01-B36,
      and makes no claim at all in C and D)

Nothing was run on a model: whole turns use a stand-in whose replies are written in the case. The shelf labels are
my own judgement. Where I allowed a second shelf after seeing the result, the case's "why" says so (the letter and
the budget to 3.2, the well to 6.3, saving money to 2.2). Part C was partly written to probe, so its rates are not a
fair sample. Part D's 60 were labelled before they were run, and its rates are the fair ones.


Worst first
-----------

1. HIGH. The library prompt offers the food shelf where the answer is "do not eat it", and OPEN then hands over
   "Cooking food so it is safe". (B85, B95, B96, B97, B100, C207, C208)
   "Is it safe to eat wild mushrooms?", "Which wild berries are safe to eat?" and "Is meat from a cow that died
   of sickness safe to eat?" all get the header "This question may be on shelf 6.2 food ... To read its lessons,
   reply with only one line: OPEN 6.2." A model that copies that line gets Keeping food and water safe and Cooking
   food so it is safe as the passages to answer from. For the cow it is "Heat kills the germs in food ... Whole
   cuts of beef 63 C", and the model is told never to contradict the passages. The whole turn with a stand-in
   confirms it (B100). The lesson that says "Never eat an animal that died of an unknown illness" is on shelf 6.4,
   and OPEN 6.4 sends it (B87, B88, B99 agree). This is the first review's mushroom fault (keeps() handing Cooking
   food) come back by another road.
   Why: open() lets a lesson through on "safe" and "eat" alone (strong 1, cover 0.5 to 0.75, both words in the
   lessons' titles), with the question's subject (mushrooms, berries, a cow that died) in none of them. The offer
   comes from a lesson-other match that misses the subject in the same way.
   Old file: nothing offered and nothing handed. The model answered from its own knowledge.

2. HIGH. OPEN sends lessons for medicines. (B80, B81, B82, B83, B98, C209)
   - "How long does insulin keep outside a fridge?": OPEN 6.1 sends The newborn baby and Poisoning (one rare word
     at 31% by weight passes the 30% bar). OPEN 6.2 sends Keeping food without a fridge and Preserving food.
   - "How should I keep my medicines in the heat?": OPEN 6.2 sends Cooking food so it is safe and Milk and eggs
     (half the words: keep, heat).
   - "How long can vaccines be kept out of the fridge?": the header itself offers 6.2, and OPEN 6.2 sends Keeping
     food without a fridge.
   - "How long does ORS keep once mixed?": OPEN 6.2 sends Fermenting (medium). OPEN 6.1 rightly sends Oral
     rehydration (B84).
   keeps() leaves medicines out (MEDW), but open() has no such rule. The comment in open() says the first review's
   insulin case was mended. For this wording it sends two other wrong lessons.
   Old file: nothing handed.

3. HIGH. keeps() hands Food lessons for an illness. (A93, C147)
   "How long does food poisoning last?" is read as food being kept ("food" ... "last"). It gets Keeping food and
   water safe, Preserving food and Cooking food. In the library prompt the header says "This question is on shelf
   6.2 food ... Lantern has opened it for you" (sure, 96%). A sick person needs Diarrhoea (diarrhea): care at home
   and when to get help.
   Old file: nothing handed.

4. HIGH. The surety does not hold for claims made from lessons. (D-sure-lessons, D-likely-lessons, D-sure-all,
   D-likely-all, D02, D17, D29 and others, C082, C097, C099, C109, C121, C133, C135, C138)
   On the 60 fresh labelled questions (questions.json):
     on shelf (sure):       20 of 23 right (87%), under 9 in 10
     most likely:           14 of 19 right (74%), under 8 in 10
     from recipe cards, MAKE, puzzles:    14 of 14 sure, 6 of 6 likely -- these hold
     from lessons (lesson-howto, health):  6 of 9 sure (67%), 8 of 13 likely (62%) -- these do not
   Over every question of mine that drew a claim (C and D, 117 claims):
     tools:    33 of 34 sure (97%); cards and MAKE 13 of 13 most likely
     lessons:  28 of 34 sure (82%); 16 of 27 most likely (59%)
     lantern-named: 2 of 6 most likely (see 5)
   The wrong "on shelf" claims:
   - "How do I put out a fire in a cooking pot?": on 6.2 food, with Cooking food so it is safe given. A pan fire
     is not in it, and "Do your homework: use what Lantern gives you below before your own memory" pushes the
     model off what it knows (a lid, the heat off, never water). High.
   - "How do I start a savings group in my village?": 6.4 farming (Saving your own seed).
   - "How do I clean rust off my tools?": 6.4 (Clean water, for animals).
   - "How do I keep records of my sales?": 6.4 (the animals' Record-keeping).
   - "How do I grow tomatoes in a dry place?": 6.2 (drying food).
   The wrong "most likely" claims:
   - soap: 6.1 (Caring for a sick person), or 6.3 (the latrine lesson)
   - charcoal: 6.1 (Poisoning)
   - "a wall that will not fall down": 1.2 (Thinking traps)
   - storing petrol: 8.3 (Working safely; Fuel, oil and safety is on 8.4)
   - a kite: 6.2
   - a fire without matches: 6.2
   - a newborn calf: 6.1, and HEALTH_CHAT hands The newborn baby (a person's)
   - a fishing net: 6.1
   - soil on a slope: 6.3
   - wiring a light switch: 8.3
   Why: the labelled how-to questions were mostly about things Lantern has lessons for. A how-to about anything
   else still finds one strong word somewhere. Then lesson-howto@<shelf> is drawn toward the kind's 86%:
   lesson-howto@8.3 says "most likely" on one question, and @2.3, @8.4 and @9.3 say "sure" on two each. The same
   holds for health@6.1 (83%), right 14 of 20 on my questions.
   The lessons handed for these are not new (SUITE_CHAT's howTo, HEALTH_CHAT). What is new is the header telling
   the model, sure, that they are the shelf, and to do its homework from them.
   Old file: the same lessons, with no claim.
   A suggestion: label how-to questions on things Lantern lacks, and count them in; name a shelf from a lesson only
   when the lesson has the question's subject (cover, not one strong word).

5. MEDIUM. A solar or paraffin lantern is taken for Lantern. (C139, C140, C141, C142)
   These four questions get "This question is most likely on shelf 0.1 Lantern's own tiles and how to use them.
   Lantern has opened it below.":
   - "My solar lantern does not charge any more. What could be wrong?"
   - "Will my lantern work with kerosene instead of paraffin?"
   - "Does the lantern have a spare wick?"
   - "Can the lantern work in the rain?"
   Nothing about Lantern is opened below, and the model is pointed at the software. A solar lantern is one of the
   commonest things this audience owns. The rule (route's "lantern-named": lantern followed by does, have, work
   and others) was right 2 of 6 times on my questions.
   Old file: no claim.

6. MEDIUM. Right answers are read as OPEN. (B61 to B75, B101)
   The reader takes "a note in brackets" with anything after it. It looks for steps only by verbs in capitals, and
   a lone digit is a class. These are read as a command:
     "OPEN 1 (the inlet valve) first, then start the pump."             -> class 1
     "OPEN 1 (inlet) first.\nThen start the pump and watch the gauge."  -> 1
     "- OPEN 1\n- Start the pump\n- Check the pressure"                 -> 1 (a bulleted list of steps; the whole
                                                                            turn sends it back, B101)
     "OPEN 1\nStart the pump.\nCheck the pressure."                     -> 1
     "OPEN 2\nthen close valve 1", "OPEN 2\nLet the water run for a minute."   -> 2
     "OPEN 3 (the drain) for 10 seconds."                               -> 3
     low: "OPEN 4 - the bottom one", "OPEN 2 (two) windows at night ...", "OPEN 2 -- then wait",
          "Open 2." and "open 2" as the whole reply, "OPEN 1 and 2.", "OPEN 2 or 3", "OPEN 1.5"
   These are valve and window answers, the pump-station shelf's own subject. The answer is not lost for good (the
   class list goes back and the model answers again), but the person waits a round and the answer can change.
   Old file: no OPEN; these replies were answers.
   A suggestion: read a class (one digit) only as the whole reply or with the class's own title; read a bracket
   only when it closes the line; count a step line in any case ("Start", "Check", "Let", "then").

7. MEDIUM. The change misses most of the food questions it is for. (A30 to A54: 16 medium, 9 low)
   keeps() is true, but nothing is handed:
   - eggs, butter, and dried, salted or smoked fish and meat, "without a fridge". Keeping food without a fridge (a
     Health-tile lesson on shelf 6.2) comes first, and the Food-tile filter then drops every passage, Preserving
     food too.
   - "how long does cooked rice keep without a fridge": the bench question with three more words.
   - goat milk: Goats & milk comes first.
   - fresh fish in the heat, porridge left out, soup overnight, "before leftover rice goes off", cooked rice kept
     for the next day: no sure passage.
   KEEPS also lacks "leave ... out", "stay out" and "how long is ... safe". A digit stops it even where the lesson
   has the answer: "at 35 degrees" is the 1-hour rule above 32 C.
   The questions it does reach, it handles right. A01 to A29 all agree, in the auto, short, full and library
   prompts: cooked food left out, leftovers, raw meat, a hot car, milk after milking, fermenting time, the bench
   row.
   Old file: nothing for any of them.
   A suggestion: let a shelf-6.2 lesson pass the filter (the shelf, not the tile), and add the missing phrasings.

8. MEDIUM. keeps() hands Food lessons to people going without, and to rationing. (A94 to A101)
   - "How long can a baby last without milk?": Feeding babies and children, and Milk and eggs. A baby not feeding
     is a danger sign. The library prompt says "on shelf 6.2", sure.
   - "How long can my family last on the food we have left?": Cooking food so it is safe.
   - "How long will our food stores last if we ration?": Preserving food, whose "dried fruit keeps about a year" a
     small model may copy.
   The exclusion catches only "without food/eating/meals", "go without", surviv and starv.
   Low:
   - pet food and pig swill
   - milk powder (Feeding babies and children)
   - a baby's bottle of milk: formula by another name, which MEDW leaves to the model
   - "How long does fruit keep?": only the dried-fruit year is handed
   Old file: nothing.

9. MEDIUM and LOW. Other wrong claims and offers. (C010, C143, C201 to C216)
   - "Is it a good idea to buy a lottery ticket every week?": "on shelf 2.2 plans", sure (MAKE plan on "every
     week"). Medium.
   - "Is there a tool to cut glass?": "about Lantern itself". The about() rule is old; the header now states it.
     Low.
   - Of 16 "may be on shelf" offers checked, 13 are off. Low each, except the three on wild food and vaccines
     (findings 1 and 2):
       the food shelf: how plants make food, a cow's water, fruit trees
       music: the speed of sound
       health: a well's depth, milk going bad, a meal keeping you full
       the earth and the weather: mutton in cold weather
       safe water: boiling meat
       living things: bread
       farming and animals: chicken soup

10. LOW. Copies of the header are not read. (B34, B35, B36)
   - "OPEN 6.2. Otherwise answer from what is below." is the header's own line, copied from OPEN on, which a
     0.8B is likely to write. It is read as nothing and shown to the person as the answer.
   - "OPEN 6.2 because the question is about food" and "OPEN 6.2 food, cooking, keeping" are not read either.


What holds (right inputs that stay right)
-----------------------------------------
- The bench rice row and 28 other food-kept questions get a Food lesson that says 2 hours (1 above 32 C), in all
  four prompts (A01 to A29).
- 33 "how long" questions that are not food being kept get no Food lesson (A60 to A92): a battery, a tyre, seeds,
  formula, breast milk, ORS, vaccines, insulin, tablets, diesel, paint, cement, manure, hatching eggs, dough,
  soaking beans, a calf, a meat chicken, seedlings, a live fish, tapeworm, a sick child. HEALTH_CHAT's lesson
  still comes first for a child with diarrhoea (A90, A91).
- OPEN is never read in the auto, short or full prompt (B76 to B79, B102).
- The command as taught is read in every dress tried (B01 to B33): bare, bold, backticks, ANSWER:, after
  <think>, title copied, a note in brackets, a decimal comma, curly quotes, a no-break space, a Windows line end,
  repeated.
- These are not read as the command: valve sequences in capitals, numbered steps, constants in code, BASIC file
  input, shop hours, recipes in capitals, a line after a colon (B40 to B60).
- OPEN 6.4 for meat from a dead animal, OPEN 6.1 for ORS, OPEN 6.2 for honey and a baby, and OPEN 7.1 for a solar
  lantern send the right lesson. A class lists its shelves.
- Assist's prompt names no shelf for a question in words. It names one for a sum.
- The claims from recipe cards, MAKE and puzzles hold their bands on fresh questions: 33 of 34 sure, 13 of 13
  most likely.
